headline: High risk: Open Interpreter’s filesystem and shell access can amplify shared-workspace prompt injection and data leakage from marketingskills outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: marketingskills writes shared skill/context files and builds on shared context, while Open Interpreter reads/writes the filesystem and can ingest clipboard/stdin content. That creates a plausible default path where attacker-controlled marketing content or skill files can steer Open Interpreter. The interaction is inferred, not directly sandboxed.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or skill directory
IF Open Interpreter consumes file or clipboard content as instructions
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable clipboard-based handoff
Require manual review of any file passed from marketingskills to Open Interpreter
Run Open Interpreter in safe mode or without auto-run
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared files

B_data_leakage.rationale: marketingskills touches marketing and product-marketing context, and Open Interpreter can read the entire user filesystem and send data to configured model providers. If the pair shares a workspace, Open Interpreter can exfiltrate files or context beyond what marketingskills intended. The blast radius includes sensitive local data and is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter is configured with access to the same directory as marketingskills outputs
IF model-provider egress is enabled for Open Interpreter
mitigations: Keep marketingskills outputs in a separate folder
Restrict Open Interpreter to a narrow working directory
Disable network egress for Open Interpreter when handling sensitive files
Rotate or isolate model-provider API keys
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem sandboxing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, and Open Interpreter also modifies git state while marketingskills supports multiple instances with shared context. In a shared repo or workspace, concurrent writes can overwrite each other or corrupt git history. The conflict is plausible in default multi-instance use and can cause irreversible work loss.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory
IF Open Interpreter is allowed to modify git state while marketingskills writes files
mitigations: Use separate working trees
Pause one agent before the other writes
Commit or stash changes before handoff
Avoid concurrent runs in the same repo
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: marketingskills is designed to build on shared context, and Open Interpreter can act on filesystem and shell outputs. If Open Interpreter treats marketingskills output as authoritative, a bad marketing claim or malformed instruction can cascade into executed commands or committed changes. The pathway exists, but verification can be added manually.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter uses marketingskills output as direct input to shell or git actions
IF no human verification step is inserted before execution
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Convert outputs into a checklist instead of commands
Use dry-run mode first
Limit Open Interpreter to read-only review
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: marketingskills handles marketing content, while Open Interpreter can access anything reachable on the local machine and may transmit context to configured model providers. If local files include regulated or residency-bound data, the pair can create retention or residency mismatches. The other agent is not cited because the compliance risk is driven primarily by Open Interpreter’s broader data reach.
conditions: IF local files accessed by Open Interpreter contain regulated or residency-bound data
IF provider-side logging or retention is enabled
mitigations: Exclude regulated folders from Open Interpreter access
Use a provider with suitable residency terms
Review retention settings before use
Keep marketing-only data in a separate workspace
requires-engineering: implement data-class routing and retention controls
